submitted.rationale: EQE kept rising as Fe increased: 0.0064% at Fe0.53 (idx 9), 0.102% at Fe0.78 (idx 3) and 0.194% at Fe0.85 (idx 0). Idx 0 is the most Fe-rich composition in the library and had the highest measured EQE. MACE puts both hematite and rutile FeSbO4 on the convex hull. MEGNet gaps are 2.08 eV for FeSbO4, 2.38 eV for FeSb2O4 and 2.77 eV for Fe2O3.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.0064% EQE. Near-1:1 rutile FeSbO4 absorbs but performs poorly.
Not measured. EQE fell steeply toward the Sb-rich side, and MEGNet gives FeSb2O4 a larger gap (2.38 eV).

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts rutile FeSbO4 essentially on hull (0.0016 eV/atom), so near-1:1 compositions should crystallize as a single phase; MEGNet HSE gap 2.08 eV < 2.7 eV photon energy, so it absorbs. Index 9 (Fe0.53) is nearest the 1:1 stoichiometry.

Support: MACE puts hematite on the hull, so Fe-rich films should be hematite plus some rutile FeSbO4. Sb doping of hematite is known to help transport. The near-1:1 FeSbO4 point (idx 9) gave low EQE, so I'm moving to the Fe-rich side (idx 3).

Against the Sb-rich side: MEGNet gives trirutile-type FeSb2O4 a 2.38 eV gap, which absorbs 2.7 eV light only weakly. Combined with the low EQE at 1:1, that points away from Sb-rich compositions. The Fe-rich trend (0.006% at Fe0.53, then 0.10% at Fe0.78) supports going further toward the hematite-rich end, so I'm measuring idx 0.
